newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil panel rejects re-election bill changes.
newsitem.headline: Brazil panel rejects re-election bill changes.

text.p: A commission in Brazil's Senate rejected a series of proposed alterations to a bill that would allow President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to run for re-election next year, a Senate official said.
The Constitution and Justice Committee earlier approved the bill which now advances to the floor of the Senate.
A first full vote in the Senate was expected to take place in two weeks' time, the official said.
As a constitutional amendment, the bill requires two three-fifths majorities for approval. It has already been approved in the Chamber of Deputies.

The legislation would allow presidents, state governors and mayors to run for a second, consecutive term, undoing a ban on re-election which dates back to the founding of the Brazilian Republic in 1889.
